title: Quarter Edge Surge Ops and All-Hands Scenario Lab v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact working plan for the quarter-edge surge exercise and the associated All-Hands run (Q2 readiness). Goal: align exec messaging, surface operational gaps (capacity, rollbacks, comms), and rehearse fallback flows under a high-throughput scenario.

Context + why now:
- We expect two sustained traffic shape experiments in Q2 as product teams enable new Preview features (catalog rollout + streaming previews).
- Historically we see 3 failure modes during spikes: autoscale lags, cache-coherency regressions, and cross-region routing surprises.
- This quarter we must prove: dedicated fallback chains, communication cadence for customers, and ops staffing for 0-2 hour P50 restoration.

High-level outcomes we want by end of lab:
1) Confirm rollback and model-fallback policies for top 5 customer routes (owned by product-hosted-api).
2) Validate an SLO-based capacity alarm threshold and attendant pager chain (on-call + escalation).
3) Produce a <3-slide exec brief and 12-min All-Hands segment that explains what happened, learnings, and ask of the company.

Proposed OKR drafts (seed for leadership convo):
- O: Ensure inference availability for customer-facing routes during surge windows.
  - KR1: Reduce median recovery time for surge incidents from 45m to 20m (eng-sre + serving-runtime).
  - KR2: Publish 3 automated rollback playbooks and test them in blue/green rehearsals (release-engineering).
  - KR3: Achieve <2% error-rate on top-10 tenant routes during a 2x traffic replay (dedicated + hosted-api).

All-Hands run of show (12 minutes total):
- 0:00–1:30: Framing (CEO) — why Q2 experiments matter to our product and customers.
- 1:30–4:30: Live trade-off vignette (product-hosted-api lead) — short demo of a traffic scenario, what we observed.
- 4:30–8:00: Ops postmortem-lite (eng-sre) — sequence, root causes identified, what we automated.
- 8:00–10:00: Ask + staffing (people ops + eng managers) — surge volunteer list, training dates.
- 10:00–12:00: Q&A (moderated, with fallback topics pre-seeded).

Rehearsal checklist (pre-All-Hands):
- Confirm demo environment (dedicated staging replica) and test data is cleared — owner: Diego (deadline: 2026-03-10).
- Run synthetic traffic replay (2x baseline) and capture latency/trace artifacts — owner: Lina (deadline: 2026-03-12).
- Prepare 3 visual artifacts for the slides: latency graph, rollback sequence diagram, staffing heatmap — owner: Priya (deadline: 2026-03-15).
- Prep fallback Q&A cards: anticipated customer questions + simple answers — owner: Ava (deadline: 2026-03-16).

Contingency scenarios (scenario lab scripts):
- Scenario A (Autoscale lag): autoscaler delays >2 minutes causing token queue growth.
  - Play: switch traffic to standby pool in same region -> enable model-quantized variant -> purge KV caches if stale.
  - Critical checks: capacity delta, model compatibility, roll-forward latency.
  - Ownership: infrastructure + serving-runtime.

- Scenario B (Cache-coherency regression): cached prefixes return stale completions for 30+ minutes.
  - Play: disable prefix serve for affected tenants, enable cold-start warming for hot prefixes, start a sticky-caching-hold for verification.
  - Ownership: serving-runtime + product-hosted-api.

- Scenario C (Cross-region routing surprise): traffic drops due to misrouted region failover.
  - Play: force routing policy to primary region with controlled throttling -> enable regional-burst capacity -> customer comms.
  - Ownership: platform-engineering + private-deployments.

Communication protocol (internal + external):
- Internal: use #incident-surge (Slack) for event chatter; ensure the first 5 messages include severity, impacted routes, immediate mitigations, and the primary on-call.
- External (customer-facing): staged comms template: "We observed degraded performance on [route]; we routed to a fallback variant and expect restoration within X hours. We will provide a post-incident summary in 72 hours." (CS owner: Maya).

Staffing plan + training slots:
- Surge rota: create a 24-hour volunteer pool split into 4-hour shifts for the first 48 hours of an incident.
- Training: 90-minute surge tabletop for engineers and support staff (target dates: 2026-03-20 and 2026-03-27).

Open questions / risks (notes-to-self):
- Do we have permission to run 2x live-traffic replay in staging clusters used by partners? (Ask: infra legal/compliance).
- Is there a cost cap for burst capacity experiments this quarter? Need finite budget and invoice owner.
- Can the telemetry dashboards render per-tenant token breakdown at 1s granularity? If not, we may lose signal during spikes.

Decision log (initial entries):
- 2026-02-12: greenlighted surge scenario lab for Q2 readiness. Owner: Exec sponsor (CTO).
- 2026-02-18: approved rehearsal dates and All-Hands segment slot. Owner: Head of People Ops.

Next steps (short):
- Sync exec alignment: 30-min working session to finalize asks for All-Hands (owner: Ava) — target: 2026-03-02.
- Create rehearsal script and record dry-run (owner: Ethan) — target: 2026-03-17.
- Publish final 3-slide exec brief and share with comms (owner: Priya) — target: 2026-03-18.

Appendix (quick refs and links):
- Example customer route list (top-10 by token-volume) -> JIRA: JIRA-OPS-987 (see linked_artifacts).
- Playbook template: /confluence/playbooks/surge-fallback-template (placeholder).

Notes: keep this doc concise, use it as the single source for rehearsal artifacts and decisions until the postmortem is published.

Unresolved: need to confirm participant list for the live demo (who will press the red button).
